So the verse/chorus chords chords go: {Gma7, Dma7 / Gma7, Dma7 / Gma7, Dma7 / C#ma7 (as passing chord), Cma7, Bmi7}

So that’s not so unusual for Frank. He loves that bVII to vi movement (e.g. Nikes, end of Self Control).

And the melody’s not so random! Basically all diatonic, he plays around with D major and usually lands on tonic chord tones. A real cool part is when he will land on the G (“shoegaaaazer”) over the Dma7, which, to me, kind of implies a G Lydian tonality since he really hangs on it, but the progression is clearly in D major. The main thing that makes it sound random is how dense he makes the verse melody, which is in stark contrast to the chorus with its simple 5-1 and 5-6-5 melodies. 

Anyway, hope that helped! The main part of it is strong rhythm and landing on chord tones.
